newsitem.title: UK: I won't be bullied, says UK Labour's Blair.
newsitem.headline: I won't be bullied, says UK Labour's Blair.

text.p: British opposition Labour leader Tony Blair said on Thursday he would not be bullied by trade unions or other interest groups seeking special favours if he becomes prime minister after the May 1 election .
"People will not be able to threaten or bully any government I lead," he told BBC Radio in an interview.

"I will be as tough as anyone has ever been. Nobody, no interest group, no pressure group, no trade union, no vested interest of any kind is going to stand in the way of me giving the British people the deal I have promised."
The Labour Party was born out of the trade union movement, but Blair has sought loosen ties with them despite the fact they are still major financiers of the party.
Blair said he had changed the party so it could resist outside pressures from interest groups.

"I have changed the Labour Party so it is not susceptible to pressures from any (groups). We changed the way our Members of Parliament are elected, we changed our relations with the trade unions, changed our policy making process...and the party is going to resist pressure from them (unions) or anybody else."
